key_insight: G-Retriever’s graph tokens become nearly indistinguishable across inputs, functioning primarily as a generic soft prompt rather than conveying graph-specific content.
engineering_relevance: Evaluate graph-token alignment with controlled interventions, not task accuracy alone, before relying on graph soft prompts to inject relational information.
method: Analyze token collapse across graph encoders, LLM families, and adaptation settings.
Replace graph tokens with mean, cross-example, or corrupted-graph tokens and compare against a learned constant prompt.
Test a two-stage procedure for non-collapsed tokens and probe what information those tokens encode and influence.
evidence_signal: Across three benchmarks, three graph encoders, and two LLM families in frozen and LoRA-adapted settings, token substitutions showed no resolved accuracy effect, while a learned constant prompt matched or surpassed G-Retriever on all three benchmarks.
watch_item: The two-stage procedure produces non-collapsed tokens with competitive performance in most cases, but token variability does not establish that the LLM uses graph information.
paper_title: On the Token Collapse Phenomenon in Textual Graph Soft Prompting
